prize_parts.citation: For a body of dream-logic fiction in Chinese that dismantles ordinary psychology, space and causality and renews the possibilities of narrative invention.

statement.case_for: Can Xue's claim rests on the distinctiveness of her voice and on formal achievement that does not depend on theme. Public knowledge of Frontier and Love in the New Millennium, and of the wider run of novels and stories, describes a fictional method that replaces conventional psychology and causal storytelling with a dream logic held consistently over decades. That is a sustained, uncompromising literary project with real imaginative and intellectual depth, in the sense of the will's idealistic direction. Her critical writing on other literatures adds a second line of intellectual seriousness. A single-writer citation is straightforward because the contribution is a personal fictional method, not a collective or topical one. After reading my colleagues' openings I keep Can Xue first. Several members reached her from different starting points, and the arguments they gave were about voice, formal commitment and imaginative autonomy, not about reputation. I treat that as a reason to test her case harder, not as evidence of merit in itself.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is range against intensity. A method this consistent may be a limit as much as a strength, and I cannot settle from the supplied description whether the later work deepens or only repeats the early dream-logic. A second reservation is access. Only part of a very large Chinese-language corpus is available in translation, and the translators' share in how the prose reads is large. I have not independently verified any text. My judgment of sentence-level achievement is therefore partly mediated, and I cannot judge the original Chinese.

responses.point: Mattson ranks Cărtărescu first for a recognisable visionary voice, a very large imaginative scale, and coherence across volumes and across prose and poetry. She asks of Can Xue whether the work evolves or merely repeats a method.
responses.response: The question about Can Xue is fair, and I cannot answer it conclusively from the supplied material. I would apply the same test to Cărtărescu, whose maximalism several colleagues, Carlberg and Palm among them, flag as a possible repetition of motifs over very long books. I agree that his coherence across prose and poetry is a real strength. But the poetry is thinly translated, so the coherence is the part I am least able to assess. I keep him as an alternative and not as my first choice. A single stable method held with rigour seems to me a stronger sign of sustained quality than scale alone, though I hold that view provisionally.

responses.point: Olsson ranks Zurita first. He argues that the long sequences Purgatory and Anteparadise turn collective suffering into memorial form with consistent ambition, and that the fit with the will's idealism rests on the depth of the work and not on its political symbolism.
responses.response: I accept the framing, and I take his own caveat seriously: the citation must rest on the poetry itself, with the landscape-scale and sky-writing interventions as context. That caveat is where I diverge. Much of the force he describes lies in acts outside the text, and in translation the verbal achievement, which is what matters under common criteria, is the hardest part for a non-Spanish reader to assess. I ranked Zurita sixth for that reason and not because the project lacks seriousness. I am willing to hear a close account of the language of the sequences that would move me. Until then the historical weight of the subject cannot carry the case.

responses.point: Sem-Sandberg ranks Cărtărescu first and Can Xue second. He credits Can Xue with a radically original voice and a project that works as imaginative and philosophical inquiry, but he notes that the unvarying method raises the question of range versus intensity and that opacity may limit breadth of significance.
responses.response: I share the worry about range and do not wish to dismiss it. My answer is that his own description, imaginative and philosophical inquiry and not stylistic experiment alone, is what separates her from a mere exercise in form. Intensity of that kind is also the basis of Marilynne Robinson's claim, which I ranked second. I would still hold Can Xue to the harder standard that opacity may limit significance, since an oeuvre that is hermetic across its whole length would weaken the case. If colleagues who know the translations more closely can point to real variation within the method, it would strengthen my position. If they cannot, I would reconsider the order of Can Xue and Cărtărescu.

responses.point: Carlberg also ranks Can Xue first. She argues that the dream logic is rigorously maintained, so the formal achievement is original and not decorative, while naming translation loss, partial corpus coverage and divided opinion on sustained quality across long works as uncertainties.
responses.response: I agree with her central claim that the rigour of the dream logic is what makes the work formally original and not decorative, and her uncertainties match mine. I would add that agreement between us is not an independent check, since we are working from the same public description and neither of us has verified the texts. Her point that opinion may divide on sustained quality across long works is the one I most want tested in discussion, because it bears on whether the novels hold up as well as the stories.

uncertainties: Only part of Can Xue's very large Chinese-language output is available in translation, and I cannot independently assess how far the translations convey the original prose.
It is unresolved whether her later work deepens or varies the dream-logic method, or repeats it.
Cărtărescu's poetry and parts of his prose are thinly translated, so my comparison of him with Can Xue rests on public reception more than on direct reading.

How non-textual interventions such as Zurita's landscape works should count under the will, and how to weigh essays, translation and scholarship against original work (Carson, Adonis, Robinson), is a question for the committee.
I have not read or verified any of these works independently, and all judgments here come from the supplied descriptions and general public knowledge.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. My own literary practice (family drama, love and obsession, WWII-era refugee fiction) is context only and shows no connection to any shortlisted writer. My professional ties are to fellow Academy and committee members, not to any candidate.
